name: vol_surface_signal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, the ratio of ATM put premium to ATM call premium tracks real-time intraday directional order flow between market participants. When institutions or hedgers aggressively buy puts for short-term protection, ATM PE premiums spike relative to ATM CE premiums, pushing the PE/CE ratio significantly above its 20-minute session baseline. At a 2-sigma intraday extreme, this put-buying burst has typically exhausted available demand — the feared event hasn't materialized — and NIFTY tends to recover over the next 30-90 seconds as market makers delta-hedge by purchasing index futures. Symmetrically, extreme call-buying (ratio z-score below -2σ) signals bullish exhaustion as speculative call demand wanes, creating a short-term bearish fade opportunity.

indicators.name: atm_ce_close
indicators.formula: option_df[type==CE, strike==atm_strike, nearest_expiry].close (asof-joined to spot bars)
indicators.purpose: Captures the current ATM call premium — together with ATM PE gives a direct real-time skew proxy without needing Black-Scholes IV computation.

indicators.name: atm_pe_close
indicators.formula: option_df[type==PE, strike==atm_strike, nearest_expiry].close (asof-joined to spot bars)
indicators.purpose: Captures the current ATM put premium — symmetric to atm_ce_close.

indicators.name: pe_ce_ratio
indicators.purpose: Put-to-call premium ratio. ATM puts and calls should be near-parity when NIFTY is near the strike; deviations reveal directional demand imbalance.

indicators.name: ratio_zscore
indicators.purpose: Normalizes the PE/CE ratio to intraday context using a 20-minute (240-bar) rolling window. WHY 20 min: intraday skew in NIFTY options fluctuates on 10-30 minute cycles tied to institutional execution windows and news digestion; shorter windows (<60 bars) produce too many false signals, and longer windows (>500 bars) adapt too slowly to regime shifts within a session. 20 minutes is not a scaled version of the original 20-day window — it is independently chosen for intraday mean-reversion timing.

indicators.name: spot_mom_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute spot momentum trend filter. WHY 12 bars (1 min): prevents fading a strong directional move that is still accelerating; the skew-exhaustion fade only works when the underlying spot move has paused or slowed, not when it is impulsive.

conditions: ratio_zscore > z_threshold (default 2.0) — extreme put-buying burst exhausted
atm_ce > 5 AND atm_pe > 5 — options are liquid and priced
VIX between 12 and 25 — option market liquid and not in crisis
buy_ce.confirmation: ratio_zscore cross above z_threshold at bar close

conditions: spot_mom_12 < trend_filter_pct (default 0.003) — spot not in strong rally
atm_ce > 5 AND atm_pe > 5 — options are liquid and priced
VIX between 12 and 25 — option market liquid and not in crisis
buy_pe.confirmation: ratio_zscore cross below -z_threshold at bar close

exit.stop_rationale: NIFTY 30-90 second fade moves typically deliver 6-12 option points when the thesis is correct; if price moves 5 pts against us within the hold window, it signals the skew extreme is genuine (not noise) and deepening — the fade thesis is invalid at that point.
exit.target_rationale: Intraday skew exhaustion fades on NIFTY cover 10-20 spot points in the first 30-90 seconds (5-10 option points at delta ~0.5); 8 points captures roughly the median reversion, with 1:1.6 risk-reward. Based on NIFTY 1-min typical move range of 3-7 option pts, 8 pts is achievable on the stronger setups.

filters.vix_filter: India VIX 12-25: below 12 implies very thin option premiums (poor signal quality); above 25 implies genuine fear event where fading put-buying is dangerous
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST: start at 09:30 to let post-open option market settle (first 15 min has erratic PE/CE pricing during gap absorption)
filters.volume_filter: both ATM CE and PE must have premium > 5 pts (ensures meaningful pricing, not stale quotes)
filters.trend_filter: spot_mom_12 bounded: don't fade into a strong established move; threshold 0.3% (30bps/min)
filters.spread_filter: nearest expiry options only — avoids mixing far-expiry pricing which distorts the ATM ratio

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — as more systematic traders monitor real-time PE/CE ratios, the extreme signal may attract faster faders, compressing the fade window from 90s to 30s

adaptation_notes: The original strategy used 25-delta OTM options and a 20-day rolling IV skew z-score, firing only 2-4 times per month and holding 60-240 minutes. Three fundamental changes: (1) ATM options replace 25-delta OTM to avoid the need for Black-Scholes IV computation — ATM premium ratio is a direct price-based skew proxy available at 5s resolution. (2) The 20-day window compresses to a 20-minute intraday window — not because of bar scaling (which would give 20 days × 375 min × 12 bars = 90,000 bars), but because the intraday thesis requires an intraday baseline; the same z-score concept applied to a session window reveals 10-30 minute order flow cycles. (3) Hold time compresses from 60-240 minutes to 30-90 seconds — we are capturing the immediate order flow exhaustion, not the multi-hour skew normalization of the original.
weaknesses: Depends on option_df having sufficient quote coverage at 5s resolution — sparse option ticks create forward-fill artifacts that distort the PE/CE ratio
ATM strike changes (every ~50 NIFTY points) create discontinuities in the PE/CE ratio series; the rolling z-score adapts but may produce false signals around ATM shifts

On days where a genuine fear event materializes (RBI surprise, geopolitical shock), the PE/CE spike is real and fading it produces large losses — the VIX filter (cap at 25) mitigates but does not eliminate this risk
The 20-min z-score window means the strategy is effectively untraded for the first 20 minutes of each session after the 09:30 start

_source.original_target: skew_z normalizes to 0.5 OR 0.5% NIFTY move in direction
